rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a change in precipitate density/distribution, while the paper varied the modulation period (λ) of multilayer coatings to control interface type (coherent, semicoherent, grain-boundary-dominated). These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies elevated temperature and steady stress, whereas the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation creep with varying loading rates. These are contradictory regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes dislocation pinning by fine coherent precipitates. The paper's mechanism involves semicoherent interfaces blocking dislocations, leading to stress-induced interfacial amorphization and a transition to diffusion/interface-slip creep. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower creep strain rates with more precipitates. The paper predicts and finds the greatest creep resistance and a minimum stress exponent for the semicoherent (λ=16 nm) multilayer, not a precipitate-rich one. The predicted property (creep resistance) and direction (improved) are general, but the specific comparison and structural mediator differ.
